rv.q: Let's just say you could hear a pin drop in this rapt house.
Ms. McDonald doesn't just channel Billie Holiday; she becomes her, with a completeness that is both luminous and devastating.

McDonald inhabits the role with such respect for the damaged character she’s playing — not to mention such uncanny vocal transformation — that what could be a fragile construct becomes an immersive drama graced with complex character shadings.
Lit by her radiance, Lady Day breaks your heart.
Her spellbinding tour de force turns a workmanlike show into something captivating, surprising and satisfying.
It’s Audra McDonald before us now, accepting heartfelt thanks for one of the most exquisite and haunting performances we?re likely to see on stage this year.
But it is her singing that is transcendent.

tn.cat: Best Sound Design of a Play

aw.sub: Won Best Actress in a Play + 1 more

cn.t: McDonald's transformative performance elevates Robertson's slender 1986 bio-play into a mesmerizing tour de force, with critics hailing her complete embodiment of a broken-down Billie Holiday as both luminous and devastating.

vs.sum: Broadway's only thrust-stage theater offers an unmatched intimate experience — no seat is more than a few rows from the action. Sightlines are excellent from every angle, though some seats face actors' backs during certain scenes.

acc.note: Elevator accessible through adjoining building. Loop technology and neck induction systems available.
